answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may post jobs or claim payments. Reputation is then attached to the bonded key, and proven fraud slashes the bond, so creating many identities does not multiply influence for free. The rule should limit voting power per bond and use audits to establish fraud; otherwise a wealthy attacker can buy a sybil majority. The attacker must tie up capital across basalt, marble, and willow identities and risks losing it.
